LESSON: PEACE AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: GOVERNANCE
Topic 5.1: Peace and Conflict Resolution
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Peace and Conflict Resolution, part of GOVERNANCE in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we embrace peace in society? 2) How could we live peacefully with others in the society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to government revenue and expenditure

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Peace and Conflict Resolution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Peace and Conflict Resolution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain ways in which the National and County Governments in Kenya spend their revenue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Peace and Conflict Resolution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of paying taxes. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Peace and Conflict Resolution in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign terms related to government revenue and expenditure

   Peace and Conflict Resolution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya,

   Peace and Conflict Resolution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain ways in which the National and County Governments in Kenya spend their revenue,

   Peace and Conflict Resolution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the importance of paying taxes. ●

   Peace and Conflict Resolution helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Peace and Conflict Resolution together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: learners collaborate with others as they design a poster on ways of promoting peace in Eastern Africa and display in class.

● Responsibility: learners proactively solve problems as they write essays on ways of promoting peace among countries in Eastern Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self- esteem: learners role-play peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in school.

● Self- awareness: learners discuss, in groups, peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Religious studies: learners discuss peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society.

Creative Arts: learners role-play in groups peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society.

Sign language dictionary, vetted digital resources, journals, flash cards and posters, adapted learner’s books and other printed resources,
